clue.text: Making shooters in mug things will get wild!

indicators.note: letters that get wild run riot, so the words in, mug and things are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An enthusiast cheers that making guns from mugs and odd bits will go down a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will get wild' rearranges the eleven letters of IN MUG THINGS.
explanation.definitionFit: Shooters is slang for guns, and the craft of making firearms is gunsmithing.

clue.text: Rat on lawn young man's best friend initially avoided

parts.note: a lawn is grass

indicators.note: the opening letter of the young dog is left out, as the word avoided applies to its start

parts.note: man's best friend is the dog, and a young dog is a pup

explanation.surface: A rat scurries over a lawn while the family dog keeps well away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially avoided' drops the first P of PUP, leaving UP.
explanation.definitionFit: To grass up is British slang for informing on someone, just as ratting on them is.

clue.text: Inn or brae running? That's a very simple decision!

indicators.note: letters that are running are set in motion and come out in a different order

explanation.surface: Choosing between a pub and a Scottish hillside is the easiest call going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' shuffles INNORBRAE; a brae is a Scottish hillside.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-brainer is informal for a choice so obvious it needs no thought at all.

clue.text: Fog and rain at the front enveloping European man

indicators.note: enveloping means the first pieces wrap around the abbreviation for European

parts.note: fog is mist

indicators.note: only the front letter of rain is wanted, as the phrase points to its start

explanation.surface: Fog and rain sweep in ahead, swallowing up a traveller from the continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enveloping' has MIST plus R wrapped around E: MIST(E)R.
explanation.definitionFit: Mister is the title used for a man, and informally a form of address to one.

clue.text: Trio strung up in deliberately violent interrogations

indicators.note: up here means in disorder, as when things are churned up, so the words trio strung are rearranged

explanation.surface: Three captives are hung up during brutal questioning sessions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' (with 'strung' riding along as fodder) scrambles TRIOSTRUNG.
explanation.definitionFit: Torturings are acts of inflicting pain, as in brutal questioning meant to extract information.

clue.text: Former capital of Moldavia is excellent to go around

indicators.note: going around means turning back on itself, so the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
A1 means first-rate, written AI in crosswords

explanation.surface: A tourist says the old Moldavian capital is a fine place to visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go around' reverses ISAI. A1 (excellent) is written AI.
explanation.definitionFit: Iasi, in modern Romania, was the capital of the principality of Moldavia for centuries.

clue.text: Clothes Heather's accidentally getting back to front?

parts.note: garb means clothes
ling is another name for heather

explanation.surface: Heather has put her clothes on back to front by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a woman's name; it is the plant, ling.
explanation.definitionFit: Garbling means jumbling words or messages, mixing up their order so the end can come out first.

clue.text: Coach pal to make final beginning of September

indicators.note: the last letter of the friend is swapped out for another letter

parts.note: a pal is a bud, short for buddy

indicators.note: only the opening letter of September is used

explanation.surface: A coach asks a friend to wrap things up as autumn begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make final' replaces the final D of BUD with S, the beginning of September.
explanation.definitionFit: A coach is a long-distance bus, a sense common in British English.

clue.text: Tan bairn's bottom after bit of bother and argument

indicators.note: after places the bairn's last letter following the other pieces
a small bit of bother is just its first letter

parts.note: a row is an argument

indicators.note: the bottom of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A child's backside gets sunburnt after some trouble and a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: A bairn is Scots for a child; its bottom is N, placed after B and ROW.
explanation.definitionFit: Tan and brown are both names for the yellowish-brown colour of sunburnt skin.

clue.text: Vets test for disease on southern tip of Falklands

parts.note: a screen is a medical test checking for disease

indicators.note: on a map the southern tip is the bottom, so the last letter of Falklands

explanation.surface: Animal doctors check for infection down at the far end of the Falklands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vets' looks like animal doctors but is the verb: checks over.
explanation.definitionFit: To vet someone is to check them carefully, just as you screen candidates.

clue.text: Old Algerian leader always backed bishops and sacred leaders

indicators.note: the leaders of the five words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A historic Algerian leader always supported bishops and religious figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' takes the initial letter of always, backed, bishops, and, sacred.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferhat Abbas was the first president of Algeria's provisional government during its independence struggle.

clue.text: Erosive changes in two rivers and an artificial lake

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters between the two river letters

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river, so two of them give two Rs

indicators.note: the letters of erosive go through changes and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Erosion reshapes two rivers and a man-made lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' shuffles the clue's own word; 'in' sets the result between the two river letters. 'changes' reads as a verb in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A reservoir is a body of water created by damming, a man-made store for water supply.

clue.text: For this, ultimate of cops gets hot food to eat later?

definitions.text: For this, ultimate of cops gets hot food to eat later?

indicators.note: the ultimate letter of cops is its last

parts.note: takeout is cooked food bought to eat elsewhere

explanation.surface: Police on a long surveillance shift pick up a takeaway to eat in the car.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: on a stakeout, the police order food to keep going.
explanation.definitionFit: A stakeout is a long police surveillance, the sort of watch where officers live on takeaways.

clue.text: Light-coloured tie worn by large European

indicators.note: the tie is wrapped around the abbreviation for large like clothing

parts.note: a bond is a tie
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A pale tie is worn by a large continental man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worn by' means the tie goes round the size letter, as clothing goes round the wearer.
explanation.definitionFit: Blonde describes fair, pale-coloured hair or things of that light shade.

clue.text: Look at what HGV driver might do with old fellow!

parts.note: a lorry driver goes to get a load to haul; HGV is a heavy goods vehicle

explanation.surface: Imagine a lorry driver picking up cargo with an old chap.
explanation.walkthrough: An HGV is a British heavy goods vehicle, a big lorry; its driver gets a load.
explanation.definitionFit: Get a load of is an informal exclamation inviting someone to look at something striking.

clue.text: Left-wing member associated with Keir originally

parts.note: pin is slang for a leg, a limb or member

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of Keir

explanation.surface: A left-leaning party member is linked to Keir Starmer from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'member' looks like a party member; it is a limb, PIN (a leg).
explanation.definitionFit: Pink is used for mildly socialist politics, a paler shade of left-wing red.

clue.text: Here there are six Genevans I'm having to get sorted

indicators.note: letters that get sorted are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Six people from Geneva need sorting out, says someone organising them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get sorted' rearranges GENEVANS and IM. The definition points to the theme: six colour code-names (White, Orange, Blonde, Pink, Blue, Brown) given to the robbers in Reservoir Dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: The film's crooks are given colour names as aliases, and the grid holds six of those assigned names.

clue.text: Mass murder? I clued it awfully after last of rum!

indicators.note: after puts the jumbled letters following the rum's final letter
the last of rum is its final letter
done awfully, the letters of I clued it are messed up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A setter admits the clue is terrible, blaming the rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' rearranges the clue's own words I CLUED IT, which then follow M. The setter's self-mockery is the disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: Multicide is the killing of many people, a rare term for mass killing.

clue.text: Call volunteers close to Mull to save island animal

parts.note: to ring is to call on the phone

indicators.note: saving means holding something in, so the island letter is kept within

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

indicators.note: the close of Mull is its final letter

explanation.surface: Volunteers are called near Mull to rescue an island creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to save' puts the island letter inside the volunteers plus Mull's last letter. The TA (Territorial Army) was Britain's volunteer army reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringtail names several creatures with banded tails, such as the ringtail possum.

clue.text: A place to pull in gay bar, dancing with fourteen?

indicators.note: dancing letters move about and land in a new order

parts.note: the answer to 14 across, the colour

explanation.surface: A gay bar with dancing, colour-themed: a spot to pick someone up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' shuffles GAYBAR with PINK. 'pull in' doubles as slang for picking someone up at a bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A parking bay is a marked space where a driver can pull in and stop.

clue.text: Be outstanding in job (for a limited period only)

definitions.meaning: a piece of work with an end date

explanation.surface: Someone told to shine in a temporary post.
explanation.definitionFit: Project as a verb means jut out; as a noun, a task with a set lifespan.

clue.text: Conservative produced a torrent of wind on radio

indicators.note: on the radio words are heard, not seen, so a word with the same sound is meant

parts.note: the wind blew hard

explanation.surface: A Tory politician blustered on air.
explanation.walkthrough: BLEW and BLUE sound the same. Blue is the colour of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue is the colour of the UK Conservative Party, so a Tory is a blue.

clue.text: Don't pick up so much stuff in Bow, being thus?

definitions.text: Don't pick up so much stuff in Bow, being thus?

indicators.note: Bow is in London's Cockney East End, where speakers drop the initial aitch

parts.words: Don't pick up so much stuff
parts.note: to pick up less sound is to hear less

explanation.surface: Someone in the East End who misses a lot of what goes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Bow' drops the H as a Cockney would; Bow is a district of London's East End. Read whole, the clue says someone without ears picks up less.
explanation.definitionFit: A creature lacking ears catches fewer sounds, which is exactly what the clue's phrase describes.

clue.text: Dryer blocked by washer at its base, getting tool

indicators.note: the towel has a letter stuck within it, blocking it

parts.note: a towel is something you dry with

indicators.note: in a down clue the base of washer is its final letter

explanation.surface: A tumble dryer jammed by a faulty washer needs a tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blocked by' places R, the base of washer, inside TOWEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A trowel is a small hand tool for digging or spreading mortar.

clue.text: Drink I knocked over that half-cut Libran got in

indicators.note: the half word gets in between the reversed letters
knocked over means turned upside down, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the ego is the I, the self

indicators.note: half-cut leaves only part of Libran, its second half

explanation.surface: A drunk Libran knocked over my drink after getting in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked over' reverses the self-word to OGE; 'half-cut' keeps the second half of Libran; 'got in' puts that inside. Half-cut also means tipsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Orange, as in orange juice or squash, is a common soft drink.

clue.text: Crap coke and drop of acid upset one doing lines

indicators.note: in a down answer upset turns the letters upside down, reading them backwards

parts.note: rot means nonsense, crap
C is slang shorthand for cocaine

indicators.note: a drop of acid is just its first letter

explanation.surface: Bad cocaine and a hit of LSD knock out someone doing lines of coke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses ROTCA. 'doing lines' suggests cocaine but means saying a script.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor delivers the lines of a script, so is one doing lines.

clue.text: Around lunchtime, woo Her Maj or hanger-on of hers?

indicators.note: around means the pieces go around the hour letter

parts.note: to court is to woo
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen
one o'clock is lunchtime, and one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Wooing the Queen at lunch, or just a flunkey of hers?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' wraps the pieces round I: lunchtime is one o'clock, and one is Roman I. ER (Elizabeth Regina) is the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtier attends a royal court, an attendant who hangs about the monarch.

clue.text: The big man in the sky is sent up by small men

indicators.note: in a down answer sent up means written upwards, read backwards

parts.words: The big man in the sky
parts.note: a jokey name for God

explanation.surface: God is mocked by little people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is sent up' reverses GOD; 'sent up' looks like mocking. Theme: Reservoir Dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogs is slang for fellows, especially rogues; in the film the robbers are the dogs.

clue.text: Baby's head gets stuck in unusually antique font

indicators.note: the baby's first letter is lodged within the other pieces

parts.note: extra means unusually, especially
something antique is old

indicators.note: the head of baby is its first letter

explanation.surface: A baby got its head stuck in an old church font.
explanation.walkthrough: 'font' looks like a baptismal basin but is a typeface. 'gets stuck in' lodges B in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra bold is a typeface weight heavier than bold, used for strong display text.

clue.text: Pale-looking player who'll make the first move?

definitions.text: player who'll make the first move?
definitions.meaning: in chess the ... player always moves first

explanation.surface: A nervous-looking opponent about to open the game.
explanation.definitionFit: White can mean deathly pale; in chess, White makes the opening move.

clue.text: Top player snapping off front tip of stud in pitch

indicators.note: snapping off removes a letter from the start

parts.note: a star is a top player

indicators.note: the front tip of stud is its first letter

explanation.surface: A leading footballer breaks a boot stud on the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' looks like a playing field; it is the black sticky stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitch is a black resinous substance, and tar is the same thick dark material.

clue.text: Full sunset aroused foremost of seducer's sexual desire

indicators.note: aroused means stirred up, so the letters of full sunset are stirred into a new order
the foremost letter of seducer's is its first

explanation.surface: A glorious sunset stirs a seducer's passions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aroused' rearranges FULLSUNSET to LUSTFULNES, then S.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustfulness is the state of being full of lust, strong physical longing.
